fact: Canadian diplomats and the Canadian Embassy in Riyadh released statements calling for the release of all peaceful human rights activists detained in Saudi Arabia.
The Saudi Ministry of Foreign Affairs published an official statement expressing disbelief in comments made by Freeland and the Canadian Embassy.
The Saudi government suspended all new trade and investment relations with Canada.
Saudi Arabia expelled Canada's ambassador, named Dennis Horak as persona non grata, and gave him 24 hours to leave the country.
Saudi Arabia recalled its envoy to Canada temporarily.
Saudi Arabia instructed staff to sell off all Canadian holdings, including equities, bonds and cash.
Saudi students studying in Canada on Saudi Arabian scholarships were ordered to relocate to another country or risk losing financial assistance.
The Saudi Grains Organization advised that it would no longer accept wheat or barley of Canadian origin.
Canadian Minister of Foreign Affairs Chrystia Freeland issued a statement via Twitter expressing Canada's concern over the arrest of Samar Badawi.
Canadian Foreign Minister Freeland responded to the expulsion of Ambassador Horak at a press conference by stating Canada will always stand up for human rights.
Saudi Arabia announced that it would put a halt to its medical programs in Canada and move all Saudi patients to other countries.
Saudi Foreign Minister Adel al-Jubeir stated that his country would not engage in negotiations until Canada retracted its original statement.
Prime Minister Justin Trudeau told reporters that he refused to apologize for his country's involvement in promoting human rights.
The state airline Saudia terminated all its flights to Toronto Pearson International Airport.
The Saudi Ministry of Education informed Saudi medical residents and fellows in Canada that they can continue in their positions.
Canada and Saudi Arabia restored their diplomatic ties.
